answers.answer: Each player takes twelve ordinary turns: the 16 spaces are four seasons of three ordinary rounds and one courtship each. Courtship has no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns’; Courtship is an event with no turns, service rotation or income.

answers.answer: Hosting order: rotate all Quarters servants to Available, then Expended servants to Quarters; resolve round-track event; resolve applicable monument and Servants’ Hall effects in either order; choose activity; invite exactly the printed gentry; provide all required service; resolve all positive favours before negative favours (otherwise choose order); optionally buy; then send used servants to Expended, played gentry to personal discard, and return activity tile to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. Only the last player advances the marker after cleanup.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure—Hosting an activity; Player Reference—Host.

answers.answer: Passing order: all servants directly to Available; all gentry in personal discard to hand; resolve round-track event then ongoing effects; choose £200 or one free full Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; last player advances the marker. Servants used for an ongoing effect are expended at turn end. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: Passing: ‘all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase’.

answers.answer: Yes, provided the special-action costs are payable: the screening level is fixed at 6.1 after step 2, before Choose Activity, and remains the screening level even if Service Help lowers actual reputation to 3.4 later. Each Service Help costs three increments and moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; it cannot take one directly from Expended Service. Four actions cost twelve increments.
answers.evidence: Reputation screening is fixed at the end of step 2; later changes do not invalidate the activity. Service Help moves one servant from Quarters to Available for 3 increments.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; otherwise their order is chosen. You cannot take a negative reputation favour first to shelter it at minimum reputation; losses cannot go below 1.1. A money penalty must be fully payable. You may use positive money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money; if short, borrow if possible, otherwise you cannot play that guest or tile.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6 and Money penalty section.

answers.answer: Borrow Money: lose 2 reputation increments, gain £100; repeatable. Service Help: lose 3 increments and move one servant from Quarters to Available; repeatable. Refresh Market: lose 4 increments for a full refresh; once per turn. At minimum reputation 1.1 you cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot move a servant straight from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special actions table; minimum reputation restriction; ‘cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service’.

answers.answer: Host the Butler’s Room hiring activity using an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two servants from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, into Expended Service; there is no fee. On its upgraded side, instead of taking up to two from supply, recruit one common servant (footman, valet or lady’s maid) from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service. Unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring—Butler’s Room.

answers.answer: A housekeeper may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman may substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman), even while that type is available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: substitution rules.

answers.answer: Acquire an underbutler only by purchasing Butler’s Pantry, which immediately puts one from supply into Expended Service. It is not immediately available: normally it moves to Quarters at your next service rotation and Available at your second subsequent rotation; passing or Refresh Service VP card can make it available earlier, and once in Quarters Service Help or the Servants’ Quarters tile can allow earlier use. An opponent cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.
answers.evidence: Butler’s Pantry and underbutler timing paragraph.

answers.answer: Market cost is the Market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier. Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. Price cannot be below £100. You cannot acquire a duplicate tile you already own. Reputation does not restrict purchasing, so you may buy a tile above your reputation.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve—normally buy; price and duplicate rules.

answers.answer: If a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into rightmost spaces. A drawn duplicate stacks on its matching Market tile, then draw again. A tile qualifying for Reserve goes straight to Reserve and you draw again. If filling multiple spaces, sort only the new tiles by ascending sorting number. Buying one tile from a duplicate stack leaves the space occupied, so no refill is triggered.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve—Refill.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service draws also go there, except Largest Wine Cellar. After courtship 2, also move Market PR1 tiles, and later PR1 draws go directly to Reserve. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. Full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships is standard, after Reserve movement; Reserve stays unchanged during refresh.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve and Refresh paragraphs; Overview confirms full seasonal refresh is standard.

answers.answer: At ordinary courtships, first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. Add tile VP for the current face-up theme category, including negative values; the currently face-up hybrid category counts. Highest score gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild for hand. If tied for highest, each tied player draws a VP card and no Fairchild is awarded. Each player discards one secret objective; shuffle simultaneous discards together and put them at the bottom of the deck. Then move first player marker anticlockwise.
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep—courtships 1–3; after courtship order.

answers.answer: Final courtship returns Fairchilds as usual, then scores tile VP across all four revealed themes; repeated categories count repeatedly, including negatives. Highest gets one VP card and a Fairchild; tie breaks by reputation level, ignoring wheel position. If still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards under the courtship tie rule. Discard the final objective; then players may take a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible, before moving marker to Wedding Bells and scoring.
answers.evidence: Final courtship (round 16).

answers.answer: End-game sources: all face-up tile VP (including negative/unused); gentry VP in hand and discard (including negatives, family and final Fairchild); fulfilled objectives; reputation level 1–7 scores 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP; 2 VP per servant of all types/locations; 1 VP per £200, rounded down; printed VP on retained unused VP cards. Highest total wins. Ties: final Fairchild holder wins; otherwise highest reputation level; if still tied, shared victory. Wheel position never breaks ties.
answers.evidence: Final VP table and victory paragraph.

answers.answer: Normally receive five secret objectives at setup and two on round 6; discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score. Extra objectives from Main Library or VP cards add to the final retained count and do not cause extra discards. Shuffle simultaneous discards together and bottom-deck them. Tile objectives require owning the named tiles at game end, not upgrading them.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards.

answers.answer: A VP card may be used immediately when drawn, on any later turn of yours, and once more after final courtship before scoring; several can be used on a turn. Reveal and discard it to take its benefit. Used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained unused cards score their printed VP; you cannot take both benefit and final VP.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: VP-card rules.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after its first use; a normal tile already upgraded remains on that side on later uses. A hybrid starts with its underlined category showing and flips after every use, alternating categories. A Queen’s Suite or Lionheart Suite hosts its front activity once, upgrades into an ongoing monument, and can never host again. Only the hybrid’s currently face-up category counts at courtship and for objectives.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects.

answers.answer: Resolve monuments and Servants’ Hall during the ongoing-effects step after the round event on a hosting turn, and after the event on a pass. Monuments grant one reputation per ordinary turn; no income at courtship, and a newly bought monument first pays on a later turn. For Servants’ Hall, place one available servant on it to reduce one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one yourself; that servant cannot also serve the activity and goes to Expended at turn end. Do not target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects—Monuments and Servants’ Hall; hosting/pass order.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite: place one footman on tile, play one casual guest from hand and provide that guest’s normal service; double all guest favours including negative ones; it upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite: housekeeper on tile, one prestige guest from hand and its normal service; double one chosen favour, resolve others normally; upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite: butler on tile, draw one prestige guest from deck to attend, with no personal guest service; double nonnegative favours, exclude negative favours from doubling; keep guest and put it in your discard at cleanup; upgrades into a monument. Each suite has a fixed count of one guest, which cannot be changed.
answers.evidence: Suite activity table and fixed guest-count rule.

answers.answer: Choose a random first player. Starting to that player’s left and going clockwise, each player chooses an available base family. Bonuses: Asquith adds Dowager Countess as a fifth family card; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York adds a footman to Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Set reputation to level 1, position 1 (1.1); stack 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max counters with 1 showing and Max at bottom; do not use 7/8 counters. Each player gets one butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman in Available Service; five starting tiles (Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour, Bowling Green) with starter/building icon showing; and Lord, Lady, Heir and Young Lady family cards. Asquith additionally gets Dowager Countess; Ponsonby starts with £300. Other families start with no money (Cavendish bonus is reputation, York’s is a footman).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2, 3 and 5.

answers.answer: For three players, Servants for Hire receives three valets, three lady’s maids, six footmen, and two underbutlers total. No butlers or housekeepers are stocked. Unused servants are returned to the box and unavailable this game.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6: one valet and lady’s maid per player, two footmen per player, two underbutlers total; no butlers/housekeepers.

answers.answer: Shuffle starter guests separately from casual guests and deal two starter guests to each player’s hand; shuffle every undealt starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and follow normal casual rules, not a separate play-time guest type.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4; Gentry section: starter guests are casual guests.

answers.answer: For four players, select one double-sided monument per player plus one, so five. Choose at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments always go in the bag and do not count against this setup selection.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: Draw until six different eligible Market tiles: PR3 or less (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set ineligible draws aside and return them to the bag after filling; stack duplicate eligible tiles in one space. Normal tiles start with upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids show underlined hybrid icon. Sort six spaces by ascending sorting number from the £300 space. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments cannot enter the opening Market.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Place Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, and one reminder token per player above the track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal the first theme face up and keep revealed themes in order through the game. Put base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild cards face up on Alderley Hall. Thus the first theme is open, and old revealed themes remain in play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9; Overview says keep revealed themes in order.

answers.answer: At start of hosting turn, the Quarters servant moves to Available Service, and the Expended servant moves to Quarters. Each moves exactly one space. An available servant left unused remains available.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 1: Quarters to Available first, then Expended to Quarters; unused available servants remain available.

answers.answer: No immediate reward if Private Study is not already upgraded at the round-event step; hosting it later that turn does not grant the missed Fair reward. An already-upgraded Study immediately gives £300 and 2 reputation. Village Fair is on standard spaces 3 and 9.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table, Village Fair; reward checked before activity choice.

answers.answer: Resolve the round-track event before ongoing effects: on a hosting turn after service rotation, or on a pass after servants and discarded gentry return. At space 6 draw two objectives and keep both secret with your other objectives. Passing players receive the event too, since events resolve on passing turns as well.
answers.evidence: Round-track events; Draw Objectives row and event timing paragraph.

answers.answer: Yes. National Holiday ignores PR on all tiles and guests when hosting, so a low-reputation player can use higher-PR tiles and guests. All other requirements still apply, including service and exact gentry counts/types.
answers.evidence: Round-track events, National Holiday row.

answers.answer: Builders’ Holiday permits any number of Market and/or Reserve purchases within funds. Finish all purchases before sliding/refilling, using one unchanged Market at its existing space prices plus modifiers (Reserve at its Reserve price plus modifier); do not refresh between purchases by special action or VP card. Market Purchase VP-card buys follow the same rules. Then refill resulting empty spaces together.
answers.evidence: Round-track events, Builders’ Holiday; Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card paragraph.

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside; leave Reserve unchanged. Refill all six Market spaces from the bag under normal refill rules, sorting by number. Only after replacement is complete return the set-aside Market tiles to the bag and mix, so they cannot reappear in the same refresh.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve—Refresh.

answers.answer: Each reputation symbol is one increment. Move clockwise to gain, anticlockwise to lose; passing position 5 to 1 raises a level, and 1 to 5 lowers a level. Minimum is 1.1; standard maximum is 7.5 (Max.5). Ignore losses beyond the minimum. At Max.5, excess reputation is lost unless immediately spent on special actions; special actions can be taken before or during a reputation favour to create room.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions.

answers.answer: Money is public, and players may not give or receive money between them in this mode. Never spend more than you have; a money penalty must be fully payable. The money supply is unlimited; use proxies if necessary.
answers.evidence: Money held is public; no transfers; supply unlimited.

answers.answer: For a ladies requirement, female family members and female guests count, so family can fill it. A casual-guest requirement requires casual guests and excludes family. You must meet exactly the printed number and types; no excess or shortfall. Family cards have no PR and need no personal service.
answers.evidence: Hosting—Invite gentry: ladies/gentlemen include female/male family; casual/prestige requirements exclude family; exact requirements. Family has no PR/service.

answers.answer: An ordinary nonscreening guest-invite favour draws one indicated-deck card, reveals it to everyone and adds it to hand (or follows an explicit larger draw count). A screening invite draws the stated number, chooses the stated number to keep, reveals only kept cards and adds them to hand. Rejected screened cards go unrevealed to the bottom of their guest deck.
answers.evidence: Gentry—Invite Guest favour and screening guests.

answers.answer: Dismissal is optional, so you need not dismiss if you have no unwanted guest. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, current activity or discard, including one drawn by an earlier favour. Family cannot be dismissed. Put the guest on the bottom of its matching deck; it is no longer yours, does not return on passing, and does not score.
answers.evidence: Gentry—Dismissal is always optional; eligible locations and consequences.

answers.answer: Lord: £200. Lady: choose either screen two casual guests and keep one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation. Lady and Heir offer choices; Dowager gives both benefits; Lord has a single benefit.
answers.evidence: Base family card favour table.

answers.answer: The Young Lady gains the admirer bonus only when a male prestige guest attends the same activity. A male casual guest does not qualify; a female prestige guest does not qualify; Charles Fairchild qualifies because he is a male prestige guest. Bonus is two reputation. She still draws one casual guest in each case.
answers.evidence: Young Lady favour and Charles ruling.

answers.answer: Charles is a male prestige guest with no PR and requires a valet; his favour gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a female prestige guest with no PR and requires a lady’s maid; her favour gives one prestige guest and two reputation. Neither is a family card: both may be dismissed under normal guest dismissal, without family immunity.
answers.evidence: Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild paragraph; Gentry dismissal rule.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and costs you one reputation. Minimum-reputation protection applies, so a player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
answers.evidence: Base gossips paragraph; minimum-reputation protection.

answers.answer: Barn grants one reputation each time you host an Estate activity. Merely owning an Estate tile or passing gives no Barn reputation.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects—Barn.

answers.answer: Ordinary rotation moves all Quarters servants to Available, then all Expended servants to Quarters at the start of hosting, each one space. Service Help costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves one servant from Quarters to Available, not from Expended. The Servants’ Quarters tile lets you use one servant directly from Quarters each turn, in addition to Available and without reputation cost; send that used servant to Expended at turn end.
answers.evidence: Service mechanisms table; Servants’ Quarters tile rule.

answers.answer: Private Study’s front activity requires a butler and two family, with no tile favour. It upgrades after use into an ongoing tile and cannot be hosted again. Its upgraded side gives £300 and two reputation only when the Village Fair event resolves (spaces 3 and 9), without staffing or hosting it.
answers.evidence: Improvements—Private Study; Village Fair event.

answers.answer: Unupgraded Main Library uses a butler and two family and draws one extra objective. Upgraded Main Library uses a butler and three family and draws one VP card. Extra objectives increase the number retained for final scoring; they do not trigger extra courtship discards.
answers.evidence: Improvements—Main Library; Objectives and VP cards.

answers.answer: The Objective VP card draws two objectives, keeps one, and returns the other to the bottom of the objective deck. It adds one retained objective to final scoring.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table—Objective.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants, including those in Expended Service, directly to Available Service, usable immediately. Service Help instead costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves one servant only from Quarters to Available, never directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table—Refresh Service.

answers.answer: Hire Servant takes one servant from Servants for Hire (not underbutler) into Expended Service. It is not immediately available for service; it must advance through service rotation unless another rule moves it sooner.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table—Hire Servant; ordinary rotation.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Guest can return one gentry, including a family member, from your personal discard to hand. If used before Invite Gentry, you may then choose that returned card to attend this activity, subject to normal requirements; returning alone does not play it.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table—Refresh Guest.

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets and lady’s maids; it excludes butler, housekeeper and underbutler. Normal service VP counts every servant of all types and locations, at 2 VP each. The ten-servant objective is 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Final VP table; servant sets.

answers.answer: Yes. Upgraded Queen’s Suite counts as a monument and as an Estate tile; upgraded Lionheart Suite counts as a monument and as a Prestige tile. Thus each can count for both monument and relevant category objectives. A hybrid counts only in its currently face-up category.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference—Monument status and category; hybrid rule.

answers.answer: Nature Group is 11 VP for Flower Room plus one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is 12 VP for Gabled Conservatory plus either Main Library or North Library. Owning the required tiles at game end is enough; they need not have been used or upgraded.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: Nature Group and Domestic Group; ownership suffices.

answers.answer: Prestige guest objective scores 1 VP per prestige guest. The every-three-guests objective counts all nonfamily guests; only each complete group of three scores, so an incomplete group earns no point. A final Fairchild counts as a prestige guest and a nonfamily guest.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference—Guest bonuses; final Fairchild and guest definitions.

answers.answer: The reputation objective awards 7 VP for reaching maximum reputation level 7, regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective awards 10 VP for at least £1200. Ordinary reputation VP depends on level only (1/3/6/10/15/21/28 for levels 1–7), and wheel position does not change reputation tie resolution; ties use reputation level.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Final VP; FAQ clarification and tie rule.

answers.answer: Both West Terrace sides require one butler and exactly three family cards. Unupgraded favour: draw one prestige guest. Upgraded favours: draw one prestige guest and optionally dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity or discard to the bottom of their appropriate decks. It remains an activity tile; it never becomes an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: Improvements—base West Terrace paragraph.

answers.answer: There is no hand or discard-pile limit. Gentry in your personal discard still belong to you and score normally; passing returns them to hand.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family.

answers.answer: You may inspect all Reserve tiles at any time and buy any one, including a tile underneath another in a stack; there is no top-only rule. Every Reserve tile is public. Normal prices, duplicate restriction and purchase limits apply.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve paragraph.

answers.answer: You may choose to host an activity or pass; hosting is not mandatory. If you lack required gentry or service for the preferred activity, choose another legal activity or pass. If no activity is possible, you must pass.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure—choose host an activity or pass; hosting step 5.

answers.answer: Yes. On a passing turn you may combine the free passing-benefit Market refresh, one paid special-action refresh (4 reputation increments), and multiple Market Refresh VP cards, each of which gives a separate full refresh. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the paid special-action Refresh Market; pass and VP-card refreshes have separate availability.
answers.evidence: Special actions paragraph: other refresh methods do not use the once-per-turn special refresh allowance; multiple Market Refresh VP cards allowed.
